description:
`defimpl Protocol, for: X` classifies X through `BuiltinValueFamily::from_name`
(src/compiler2/world.rs:1917, enum at world.rs:2277, Ty minting at
`builtin_value_family_ty`, world.rs:2300). That enum knows six names: List,
Integer, Float, Atom, Binary, Map. Anything else routes to
`nominal_impl_target_ty` (world.rs:2314) and is minted as an opaque nominal type.
When a call site then feeds a real tuple, no dispatch arm matches and
materialization asserts.

## Repro -- the compiler PANICS

    defprotocol Sizer do
      fn size(value)
    end

    defimpl Sizer, for: Tuple do
      fn size(value), do: 42
    end

    fn main(), do: dbg(Sizer.size({1, 2}))

    $ ./target/debug/fz2 interp tuple_min.fz
    thread 'main' panicked at src/compiler2/jobs/artifact.rs:153:6:
    product materialization should have complete call edges after waits

Identical panic on `run` and `build`. Changing only `for: Tuple` to `for: List`
(and the argument to a list) prints `42`.

ELIXIR ACCEPTS IT. The same protocol and impl print `42`.

## Family sweep, one impl per name

    works : List, Integer, Float, Atom, Binary, Map
    panics: Tuple, BitString, Function, Any

`for: Tuple` is indistinguishable from `for: SomeUndefinedModule` today -- both
panic the same way -- which also says the nominal fallback has no diagnostic for
an unresolvable impl target.

Elixir's built-in protocol targets are Atom, BitString, Float, Function,
Integer, List, Map, PID, Port, Reference, Tuple and Any. fz spells BitString as
`Binary`.

## Two things to settle, in order

1. THE CRASH. A `defimpl` target the compiler cannot dispatch on must be a
   diagnostic, never an `.expect()`. That covers both the missing families and
   genuinely unknown names.
2. THE REGISTRY DUPLICATION, which was this ticket's original subject.
   `BuiltinValueFamily` and `resolve.rs:109 CONSTRUCTORS` both mint a Ty from a
   recognised builtin name, keyed independently -- capitalised
   protocol-impl-target names versus lowercase type-annotation names. Per
   [[feedback_fold_concordant_ideas]], decide whether these are one registry
   with a name-domain field, or legitimately two with the reason recorded at
   both sites. `map` was already in `BuiltinValueFamily` before fz-usm.3 added
   `map` to `CONSTRUCTORS`; the drift is real and directional.

Absent from `BuiltinValueFamily`, each needing a yes/no rather than a blanket
answer: Tuple (yes -- Elixir dispatches on it and it crashes today), BitString,
Function, Any, Bool, Nil, Pid, Ref, Resource, Cpointer, Utf8, Never.

## What the old ticket got wrong

It described the Tuple case as falling through to the nominal branch and being
"treated as an opaque nominal type" -- right about the mechanism, but it
understates the consequence: the compiler panics rather than mis-dispatching or
diagnosing. It also framed the whole ticket as an open design question; the
Tuple half is not a question, it is a crash on a program Elixir accepts. Line
numbers ~3190-3247/~3216/~3240/~2878 have shifted to ~2260-2314/1917/2310/2314.

## Checks

- A fixture with `defimpl P, for: Tuple` dispatching on a tuple value passes on
  interp, run and build -- or the name is documented as an intentional gap the
  way fz-usm.6 documents `tuple`'s absence from CONSTRUCTORS.
- `defimpl P, for: SomeUndefinedModule` produces a diagnostic, not a panic at
  jobs/artifact.rs:153.
- world.rs's builtin-target name table and resolve.rs's `CONSTRUCTORS` are
  either one table, or two with the reason stated at both sites.
title: defimpl for Tuple panics the compiler on all three lanes; BuiltinValueFamily is missing Tuple, BitString, Function and Any
